c.tagline: China's medieval maritime Silk Road emporium of temples, mosques, and arcade streets.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about ¥10; most locals book via Didi and pay by Alipay/WeChat QR, so carry cash or set up mobile pay — some drivers cannot take foreign cards or make change for large notes.

emergency.note: 119 for fire; English-speaking operators are limited, so hotel staff can help translate.

hood_landmark.Xunpu Village: Xunpu Village oyster shell houses, Quanzhou

hood_desc: The living heart of the UNESCO old city (Licheng), a 1,300-year-old street of temples, snack stalls, and lantern-lit lanes anchored by the twin-pagoda Kaiyuan Temple; the best base for first-time visitors.

A restored heritage street around the 1009 Qingjing (Ashab) Mosque — the oldest Arab-style mosque in China — and the Guandi Temple, mixing Song-era stone architecture with tea houses and Minnan snacks.
China's longest continuous arcade (qilou) shopping street, a colonnaded stretch of shops, old pharmacies, and street food running straight through the old town.
Quanzhou's modern downtown around Fengze Square and Puxi Wanda Plaza, home to the city's newest malls, business hotels, and nightlife; convenient but far less historic than the old city.

A fishing village at the mouth of the Jinjiang River famous for its oyster-shell houses and the 'Zan Hua' flower-crown headdresses worn by Xunpu women; a photogenic half-day escape about 10 km from the old town.
lodging: Quanzhou Grand Temple Hotel (West Street Kaiyuan Temple)
Jinjiang Inn Quanzhou West Street Kaiyuan Temple

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as everywhere in mainland China.

transit.pay: Pay buses and the BRT with a local transit card, a QR code via Alipay/WeChat, or a contactless bank card; single rides run about ¥1-¥2. Foreign visitors can link an international card to Alipay or WeChat to pay by QR.
transit.hours: The BRT and main bus lines run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM, with taxis and Didi filling the late-night gap.
transit.note: Quanzhou has no metro; getting around relies on an elevated BRT busway, an extensive city bus network, taxis, and Didi ride-hailing.

bus: Intercity coaches to Xiamen, Zhangzhou, and Fuzhou

car.idp: Not recognized (a Chinese driving license is required)

ferry: Historic Maritime Silk Road wharves at Houzhu and Shihu ports (cargo and local passenger services)
train: Quanzhou Railway Station (high-speed rail on the Fuzhou-Xiamen line to Fuzhou, Xiamen, and Shenzhen)

transit.m: Airport shuttle / city bus to downtown and the railway station (~30-45 min)
Taxi to the West Street old city (~¥40-70, 20-35 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; a service charge may be added at high-end hotels and restaurants.
